prompt_en: This winter clothing photograph shows a woman whose face and hair are guided by the supplied image, wearing winter clothing in connected layers. Her short dark bob has fine wispy bangs, brown eyes, softly rounded cheeks and natural rose lips. At the threshold of a timber potting shed in a snow-covered orchard, she has just brought a bare apple branch inside and is attaching a small paper label before returning it to a propagation box. The branch rests horizontally on a waist-high wooden workbench below her chest, its snowy twig tips extending toward the open doorway. Her left fingertips press the branch gently against the bench, while her right thumb and index finger pinch the ends of a loose cotton string already looped around the branch and through the label hole; the label hangs below the branch. Her elbows stay bent near her own torso, her wrists hover above the worktop, and her feet support her relaxed upright stance behind the bench. Her concentrated eyes follow the knot; her slightly parted lips and softened cheek in the warm doorway light give the moment a quietly attractive, approachable presence. She wears an oatmeal wool cable-knit cardigan whose upper front edges fall open over the vest. Near its lower hem, one wooden button on the cardigan's left front edge passes through a buttonhole in its right front edge, joining those two edges of the same cardigan while the upper chest remains open. Raised interlacing cable columns curve over and under one another across the cardigan body and sleeves, separated by recessed stitch channels; individual knit loops and soft wool fibers catch the light on the ridge crests. Separate narrow parallel rib-knit columns finish the cardigan cuffs, lower hem and open front edges. Beneath the cardigan is a pine-green sleeveless Fair Isle wool vest: small cream and rust geometric colorwork stitches repeat in horizontal bands across its exposed chest, with each motif sharing the continuous knitted ground rather than floating above it. A white cotton shirt is the innermost layer, its pointed collar rising above the vest neckline, a narrow shirt cuff emerging below each cardigan cuff, and a thin straight shirt hem showing below the vest and open cardigan. The collar, cuffs and hem belong to that same underlayer, with the cardigan outside the vest and the vest outside the shirt. A long charcoal rib-knit scarf passes behind her neck; its two ends descend along the outer sides of the open cardigan, leaving the center chest and vest motifs visible. Long parallel raised ribs and recessed channels run down the scarf, distinct from the crossing cable relief of the cardigan. Dark wool trousers extend beneath the shirt hem. The open shed door frames blue snow and orderly rows of bare orchard trees behind her, while a small propagation box with other labeled twigs sits at one side of the workbench. Snow crystals cling to the branch ends, and a damp mark beneath them links the recent outdoor cold to the current indoor task. A vertical three-quarter photograph runs from the crown of her head to mid-thigh, showing both hands and the full exposed cardigan front, vest chest, scarf ends and layered hems. The camera sees her from a gentle front three-quarter position at chest height, close enough to resolve the knit structures; a natural 50mm perspective keeps her body and tabletop connected. Cool daylight from the open doorway and warm side light inside the shed separate pale wool relief, flat geometric stitch colors and crisp cotton edges. Her face remains readable within the selected crop, with her eyes and natural skin texture in focus. Her right hand and its contact with the string remain sharply recognizable against the workbench. The orchard setting remains recognizable through the open shed door, with softer rows of bare trees behind. The scene feels inhabited and observant, its winter fashion understood through the differing tactile surfaces and the small useful action happening within them.
